title: Grade 8 Science — Tue, Jun 24
description: Force and Pressure — Day 2 of 5: Pressure — definition, formula, factors
subject: science

questions.question: Pressure is defined as:
options: Force ÷ Area (P = F/A) — the force applied per unit area
questions.explanation: Pressure = Force ÷ Area = F/A. SI unit = Pascal (Pa) = N/m². Pressure tells us HOW CONCENTRATED the force is. Same force over a smaller area = greater pressure. Greater area = less pressure.

questions.question: A force of 100 N acts on an area of 5 m². Pressure =
questions.explanation: P = F/A = 100 ÷ 5 = 20 Pa (pascals). SI unit of pressure = Pascal (Pa) = Newton per square metre (N/m²). Named after Blaise Pascal.

questions.question: Why does a sharp knife cut better than a blunt knife (same force applied)?
options: Sharp knife has a smaller edge area → same force over less area → greater pressure → cuts more easily
questions.explanation: P = F/A. Sharp edge: very small contact area → huge pressure at tip → penetrates material easily. Blunt edge: larger contact area → same force spread over more area → less pressure → harder to cut. This is why needles, blades, and pins have sharp points.

questions.question: A brick weighing 200 N can be placed on two different faces: Face A (0.05 m²) and Face B (0.2 m²). Which produces greater pressure and why?
options: Face A (smaller area → P = 200/0.05 = 4,000 Pa vs Face B: 200/0.2 = 1,000 Pa)
questions.explanation: Same force (weight = 200 N). Face A: P = 200/0.05 = 4,000 Pa. Face B: P = 200/0.2 = 1,000 Pa. Smaller area → greater pressure. This is why buildings have wide foundations — spread the weight over large area → less pressure on soil → no sinking.

questions.question: Why are wide, flat foundations used for heavy buildings?
options: Larger foundation area → less pressure on soil (P = F/A, larger A → smaller P) → prevents the building from sinking
questions.explanation: Building weight → downward force. Wide foundation spreads that force over large area → P = F/A, large A → small P on soil. Soil can support this without compressing. Narrow foundation → concentrated force → high pressure → soil collapses/building sinks. Same principle as snowshoes.

questions.question: Pressure in fluids (liquids and gases) acts in:
options: All directions — fluid pressure acts equally in all directions at the same depth
questions.explanation: Pascal's principle: fluid pressure at any point acts equally in ALL directions — up, down, sideways. This is why a hole in a submarine leaks equally powerfully whether on top, bottom, or side at the same depth. Unlike solid pressure, fluid pressure is non-directional.

questions.question: Liquid pressure at depth h is given by P = hρg. This means pressure depends on:
options: Depth of liquid (h), density (ρ), and gravity (g) — not volume or container shape
questions.explanation: P = hρg. Pressure increases with depth (h ↑ → P ↑), with density (denser liquid → more pressure), and with gravity. The volume or shape of the container does NOT matter — only the depth to the point of interest. That's why submarines crush at great ocean depths.

questions.question: Atmospheric pressure exists because:
options: The weight of air above any point — the atmosphere is ~100 km thick; all that air's weight creates pressure on everything at Earth's surface
Gravity has no effect on air
questions.explanation: Atmosphere = layer of air above Earth (~100 km). All this air has mass → weight → exerts downward pressure. At sea level: ~101,325 Pa = 1 atmosphere (atm). Decreases with altitude (less air above). Mountains: lower pressure → harder to breathe. Measured with a barometer.

questions.question: A diver goes deeper underwater. What happens to the water pressure on them?
options: Pressure increases — P = hρg, as depth h increases, pressure increases proportionally
Pressure depends only on body size
questions.explanation: P = hρg. As depth (h) increases → pressure increases linearly. At 10 m depth in sea water ≈ 2 atm (1 atm water + 1 atm atmosphere). Every 10 m adds ~1 atm. Deep sea creatures are adapted to survive enormous pressures (thousands of atm at trenches).

questions.question: Camels have broad, flat feet. This is an adaptation because:
options: Broad feet spread the camel's weight over larger area → less pressure on sand → camel doesn't sink (P = F/A, large A → small P)
Camels' feet are flat for walking on water
questions.explanation: P = F/A. Camel's large weight distributed over broad, flat foot pads → less pressure per unit area on sand. Sand can support this → camel walks without sinking. Compare to a person in stilettos on sand — high pressure → sinks. This is a natural application of pressure principles.

questions.question: Why do army tanks have broad caterpillar tracks?
options: Large track area → the tank's great weight is spread over large area → less pressure on ground → tank doesn't sink in mud or soft terrain
questions.explanation: Tank: very heavy. Broad caterpillar tracks: very large contact area with ground. P = F/A → small P despite large F. Tank can traverse soft mud without sinking. Also why tractors, bulldozers, and snowcats have wide tracks.

questions.question: A hydraulic jack uses Pascal's principle. A small force on a small piston creates large force on a large piston because:
options: Pressure is transmitted equally through the fluid (Pascal's principle) — same pressure on large area = large force
questions.explanation: Pascal's principle: pressure applied to enclosed fluid transmits unchanged to all parts. F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂. If A₂ >> A₁, then F₂ >> F₁. This is mechanical advantage. Applications: hydraulic brakes in cars, hydraulic jacks, hydraulic presses, dentist's chairs.

questions.question: SI unit of pressure is Pascal (Pa). 1 Pa = 1 N/m². Atmospheric pressure at sea level ≈
questions.explanation: Standard atmospheric pressure = 101,325 Pa ≈ 1 atm. This equals the weight of a 10 m column of water per unit area. Blood pressure is measured in mmHg. Pressure of a gentle breeze ≈ 1–10 Pa. Atmospheric pressure is enormous — we don't feel it because it acts equally in all directions.

questions.question: A student pushes a drawing pin into a board. Which end (sharp or flat) exerts greater pressure on the board?
options: Sharp end (needle tip) — extremely small area → enormous pressure despite modest finger force
Both equal — same force acts throughout
Depends on the material of the board
questions.explanation: Same force passes through the pin (Newton's 3rd law — force through solid body is transmitted). Sharp tip: area ≈ 0.0001 cm² → pressure = F/0.0001 = huge. Flat head: area ≈ 1 cm² → much less pressure. The concentration at the sharp point (small area) → penetrates the board. Flat side you push stays comfortable.

questions.question: Which correctly summarises the relationship between pressure, force, and area?
options: P = F × A (more area = more pressure)
P = F / A (more area = less pressure; less area = more pressure)
P = A / F (more force = less pressure)
questions.explanation: P = F/A. Key relationships: (1) Same force, smaller area → greater pressure. (2) Same force, larger area → less pressure. (3) Greater force, same area → greater pressure. Applications: knives (sharp = small A), snowshoes (large A for snow), needles, buildings (wide foundation = large A).
